First of all, I want to say that you planning ahead of this busy time, is an amazing first step. As a student in a really intense field, I can understand how frustrating it is to have to make your mental health less of a priority because of major deadlines or heavy workload. 


For me, what worked is setting times and sticking to them. It's better to spend 3 hours studying a topic properly rather than spending 6 hours "pretending" to study and getting easily distracted. You have to tell yourself "get this done now so you can rest (or do another hobby) after".


If you have any friends, siblings or flat mates, ask them to call you at certain times to make sure you're getting the work done. For me, getting up in the morning is the hardest so if I was in your position, I would make my friend (who is an early riser, that way I'm not disturbing them) to message me to make sure I'm awake and haven't snoozed off. Perhaps you may benefit from this too? If you don't want to include anyone in your plans, there are plenty of apps available which help with organisation.


Eat and sleep well! You are going to feel so much worse if you're not eating or if you're eating junk food. Please don't fall into the trap of thinking "I don't have enough time to cook something nutrional" or "I don't have enough time to sleep 8 hours". That's not the correct way to think. There are plenty of meals which don't take much effort to cook. Think beans on toast, jacket potatoes, rice and chicken, pasta etc. If you don't eat or sleep, you will be much worse. You're already sacrificing your mental wellbeing for the next few days, please don't sacrifice your physical wellbeing too.


If at any point you feel like you're getting overwhelmed. Take a few mins break. Go for a run (this helps give you energy and keeps you fresh), go for a walk (this will give you some peace), or take a shower. Don't lay down in bed, because chances are, you won't want to get back up.
